status: DRAFT, not in force (no run or lc job until prereg.json is committed)
title: Function-class ablation for the shared bias-only correction g in I = I_card x exp(g)

questions.Q1: Does the held-out gain of the shared bias-only correction depend on the function class of g?
questions.Q2: Is there a class with fewer trained values than M_bias (1765) whose held-out RRMS is not higher than M_bias by more than the margin, and does it have a lower RRMS?
questions.Q3 (secondary): How does the held-out gain of the two best classes change with the number of training devices (2, 4, 8, all) on the two largest datasets (TU Delft 4.13 K, NIST 4 K)?

background: I3-2 F2 on sky130 77 K, GMR vs C0_refit: width 8 0.759, width 32 0.777, 3-16-1 0.770, seed sets 5-9 / 10-14 / 15-19 0.771 / 0.779 / 0.771; GMR vs the I3-2 M_bias 0.988-1.083, every CI includes 1.
I5-1 IHP measured 300 K: GMR(M_bias, C0_refit) 1.214 [1.008, 1.537]; means M_bias 0.0203, B3_d3 0.0214.
I8-1 NIST 4 K: GMR(M_bias, C0_refit) 0.806 [0.758, 0.864]; GMR(M_bias, B3_d3) 0.981 [0.961, 1.000] (27/53); B3_d3 gives 91% of the M_bias log gain.

The poly2, poly3 and gp contrasts are known on the datasets where they are stored (retrospective part); the const, lin, poly4, poly5, gam, mlp8 (except sky130), mlp16_s1, mlp32 (except sky130), mlp64 results are not known. All datasets are development sets; no TEST split is loaded.

lin.form: g = tanh(c0 + c1 u' + c2 v') per polarity (u', v' standardized)

gam.form: g = tanh(c + B(u) a + B(v) b + (B(u) p)(B(v) q)) per polarity; B: 8 cubic B-splines, uniform interior knots on the training range of u = |Vgs|/VDD and v = |Vds|/VDD, inputs clipped to that range; interaction rank 1
gam.training: fit_gam: E1 loss + 1e-4 (|a|^2 + |b|^2 + |p|^2 + |q|^2); c, a, b, q start at 0, p at N(0, 0.1^2) (torch generator seed 0)

mlp16.training: stored I3-2 / I5-1 / I6-1 / I8-1 / F2 M_bias (reference, not retrained)

mlp16_s1.form: member 0 of the stored M_bias fold model (seed 0)
mlp16_s1.training: none (members are trained independently from torch.manual_seed(seed) on the same batch; member 0 equals the 1-seed fit with seed 0, unit test)

gp.form: I4-1 B4: GP posterior mean of ln|I_meas / I_sim| on (is_pmos, u, v), ARD squared exponential + white noise, constant mean, type-II ML; 2000 training points per fold (equal share per device)
gp.training: fit_gp (alpha vector 2000 + 6 hyperparameters; the 2000 x 3 stored inputs not counted)

protocol.folds: as the stored runs: sky130 77 K, NIST and IHP measured leave-one-device-out (IHP measured trains within class LV / HV); TU Delft leave-one-group-out (7 groups); GF180 / IHP tiers b and c leave-one-geometry-out (16 geometries x 3 sets)
protocol.training_records: the stored starting-card records of the fold's training devices, in the stored training order (load order; NIST sorted by tag); NIST records with non-finite simulated points excluded (amendment A1 of I8-1) and scored as failed in every class
protocol.training: E1 loss (mean over devices of the paper per-device RRMS of I_sim x exp(g)) + L2 1e-4 on non-intercept coefficients / weight matrices; Adam lr 3e-3, 2000 full-batch steps, float64, 1 torch thread; zero-initialized output (poly, gam: zero coefficients; MLP: zero last layer); GP: type-II ML (I4-1 B4 settings)
protocol.heldout_refit: ngspice_fit.polish from the stored starting card, max_nfev 400, irls_rounds 2, diff_step 0.01, g frozen in the loop, through the dataset driver's own refit function (I4-1 refit_task for sky130 and pdk2, I5-1 / I6-1 / I8-1 refit_task otherwise)
protocol.score: strict paper RRMS of I_card x exp(g) with the frozen inclusion stored on the record; a non-finite included curve scores NaN (failed)
protocol.simulators: ngspice-41 arm64 (sky130, NIST, TU Delft, GF180); Homebrew ngspice-46 + PSP 103 OSDI (IHP simulated and measured), as in the stored runs

reuse_plan: Starting-card records: E1 real_dev (+ direct43_r3_fd params), E1 {gf180,ihp}_c_set{0,1,2}, I3_2/followup/f2_{gf180,ihp}_b/records, I5_1/start/records_{T}K, I6_1/start/records_{T}K, I8_1/start/records. No starting fit is rerun.
Stored per-device rows (listed per dataset) enter the statistics unchanged.
mlp16_s1: member 0 of the stored M_bias fold model (corrections.json key 'M_bias|<fold>'); only its held-out refits are new.
New work per dataset: training of the classes without stored rows on each fold, and one held-out refit per class and held-out device.
Reproduction check: poly3 (C0_refit on tier b) retrained and refit on the first 2 held-out devices of each dataset; max |RRMS - stored| <= 1e-9 required.

statistics.per_dataset: GMR(X, Y) = exp(mean over held-out devices of ln(RRMS_X / RRMS_Y)) over devices with both values finite (failures counted separately); 95% percentile CI from 20000 device-bootstrap resamples (default_rng(0)); geometry / group cluster bootstrap reported for tier b / c and TU Delft
statistics.pooled: equal-weight pooled GMR over the primary datasets: exp(mean over datasets of the per-dataset mean log ratio); CI from 20000 stratified resamples (devices resampled within each dataset)
statistics.multiplicity: 12 primary contrasts GMR(X, mlp16), X in {const, lin, poly2, poly3, poly4, poly5, gam, mlp8, mlp16_s1, mlp32, mlp64, gp}; Bonferroni: two-sided percentile CI at level 1 - 0.05/12 (tails 0.208%, about 42 resamples each). Every other interval is a 95% interval, labelled descriptive.

decision_rule.labels: from the Bonferroni CI of the pooled GMR(X, mlp16): 'beats' if upper < 1; 'worse' if lower > 1; 'equivalent' if the CI lies in [1/1.03, 1.03]; 'non-inferior' if upper <= 1.03; else 'inconclusive'
decision_rule.Q1: 'class-dependent' if at least one class is 'beats' or 'worse'; 'no class dependence detected' if all 12 are 'equivalent'; else 'inconclusive'
decision_rule.Q2: candidates: classes labelled 'beats', 'equivalent' or 'non-inferior' with fewer trained values than mlp16 (1765), point GMR(X, mlp16) <= 1.05 on every primary dataset, and no more failed devices than mlp16 on any primary dataset. Answer: the candidate with the fewest trained values (tie: lower pooled GMR), or 'none'. 'beats with fewer parameters' if that candidate is labelled 'beats'.
decision_rule.capacity_curve: pooled GMR(X, C0_refit) (95%) against the number of trained values, reported for every class

secondary: S1: the rule on the six primary + simulated tier c datasets (Bonferroni level).
S2: per-dataset GMR(X, mlp16) and GMR(X, C0_refit) for every class and every dataset (95%).
S3: cluster bootstrap of the primary pool (TU Delft groups).
S4: margin sensitivity: labels at margins 1.02 and 1.05.
S5: fraction of the M_bias log gain retained, ln GMR(X, C0_refit) / ln GMR(mlp16, C0_refit), on datasets where the stored GMR(mlp16, C0_refit) CI upper bound is < 1.
S6: null control (tier b): GMR(X, C0_refit) for every class; a class with CI upper < 0.95 on tier b is reported.
S7: final training loss per class and fold; g maps on a 41 x 41 grid per polarity (fold mean).
S8: other temperatures (IHP measured 233 / 343 / 398 K, TU Delft 295.0 K).

learning_curve.classes: the two classes with the lowest pooled GMR(X, C0_refit) on the primary pool; GMRs within 0.005 count as tied and the class with fewer trained values ranks first (select_lc_classes); chosen by the decide output before any learning-curve job
learning_curve.subsets: per fold, 3 subsets of the fold's training devices; polarity-stratified (n/2 nMOS, n/2 pMOS; shortfall filled from the other polarity); default_rng([20261021, n, r, fold index]) on the sorted tags (training_subsets)
learning_curve.statistic: per held-out device, exp(mean over the 3 subsets of ln RRMS); per dataset GMR(X_n, C0_refit) and GMR(X_n, X_all) with 95% device-bootstrap CIs; GMR(class A_n, class B_n) per n. Descriptive; no decision.

validity.V1: reproduction: max |RRMS - stored| <= 1e-9 for the poly3 (tier b: C0_refit) rerun on 2 held-out devices per dataset; a dataset failing V1 is excluded and reported
validity.V2: failed devices per class and dataset reported; a class with more failed devices than mlp16 on a primary dataset is not a Q2 candidate
validity.V3: simulator timeouts per job reported (I6-1 10 s per process, I8-1 timeout handling unchanged)
validity.V4: the stored rows used are exactly the stored values (read, not recomputed); mlp16_s1 g equals member 0 of the stored model

compute.method: Refit CPU-s = n_heldout x (number of new refit classes) x mean single-process runtime of the stored M_bias held-out refits of the dataset (GP refits: stored I4-1 B4 mean, else corrected refit + 30 s), + 2 reproduction refits. Training CPU-s = sum over folds of (seconds per training point per Adam step per member, measured in the smoke on the sky130 77 K training sets) x training points of the fold x 2000 steps x members; GP 30 s per fold (I4-1 timing, 2000 points, 200 L-BFGS-B iterations). Wall time on 6 workers at 85% efficiency. Calibration: the smoke cost of the 16-wide MLP (0.33 us per point-step) gives 10 s (sky130), 17 s (NIST), 52 s (GF180 c) and 64 s (TU Delft) per seed task; the stored I3-2 / I8-1 / I6-1 pool timings give about 10, 15, 55 and 51 s.

learning_curve.training: n <= 8 training devices: a 5-seed 16-wide MLP costs about 1.6 n s (NIST) and 7 n s (TU Delft) per training; at most about 1 CPU-h (NIST) and 0.6 CPU-h (TU Delft) for two classes

notes: Training, not refits, dominates for the 5-seed MLP classes: mlp32 and mlp64 are about 45 of the 70 CPU-h of the full set (mlp64 alone 5.2 CPU-h on NIST, 4.9 on each tier c dataset, 2.6 on each TU Delft temperature). For const, lin, poly2-5, gam and mlp16_s1 the refits dominate.
Primary pool alone: about 19 CPU-h, 3.8 h wall on 6 workers.
NIST is leave-one-device-out (53 folds), so every class is trained 53 times.

smoke.what: sky130 77 K, held-out nmos_L0p15_W1p6 and pmos_L0p35_W0p55 (2 folds, training on the other 11 devices), all 13 classes trained with 200 steps, MLP seeds (0, 1), mlp16_s1 = member 0 of the smoke mlp16, GP 300 points / 20 L-BFGS-B iterations, held-out refit max_nfev 60, irls 1; 4 workers. Code check only; not used for any conclusion.
smoke.note: gp on pmos_L0p35_W0p55 gives 5.14 with 300 points and 20 iterations (reduced settings).

code.driver: scripts/research/explore/i9_2_classes.py (modes plan, smoke, run, decide, lc)

queue_plan_not_queued: I9_2_run_<dataset> for the 4 primary datasets (about 3.8 h wall), then I9_2_decide_primary
I9_2_run_<dataset> for gf180_c, ihp_c (about 3.8 h), other temperatures (about 1.9 h), tier b (about 4.2 h, or a reduced class set)
I9_2_decide, then I9_2_lc_tudelft_4K and I9_2_lc_nist_4K (about 1 h)
one compute-heavy job at a time; 6 workers, 1 torch thread each
open_questions: OQ1 primary pool: the 4 measured datasets (draft) or the 6 datasets including simulated tier c.
OQ2 margin 1.03 (draft) and the per-dataset limit 1.05; the F2 seed sets alone moved GMR vs the I3-2 M_bias by 0.988-1.083 on sky130 77 K (12 devices).
OQ3 reference replicate: add mlp16 with seeds 5-9 on the primary datasets (about 4 CPU-h) to measure the run-to-run spread of the reference itself.
OQ4 parameter count: total over the 5 members (draft; mlp16 1765) or per member (353); under per-member counting mlp8 (113) and gam (66) stay below, mlp16_s1 equals the reference.
OQ5 gam settings (8 cubic B-splines, rank-1 interaction, L2 only, no smoothness penalty).
OQ6 poly4 / poly5 use monomials in standardized u, v (as B3); 2000 Adam steps may not converge for degree 5; alternative: Legendre basis or 4000 steps for all classes.
OQ7 tier b null control: full class set (about 4.2 h), a reduced set {const, lin, poly3, gam, mlp16_s1} (about 1 h), or drop.
OQ8 the 20 I7-1 simulated datasets are excluded (about 1-2 h each).
OQ9 learning curve: add mlp16 as a fixed third class if it is not among the two selected; 3 subsets per size.
OQ10 equal dataset weight (draft) or device-count weight in the pooled statistic.
